beats.narration_text: Konnichiwa. This is Liam, in for Bear. To see how your team uses Claude Code, you might just ask Claude. But one chat only sees its own session. So the real question is how to track Claude Code on a dashboard.

show.event: types 'How do I track Claude Code by asking Claude?'
backspaces 'by asking Claude' -> 'on a dashboard' on the spoken correction

props.text:
How do I track Claude Code
by asking Claude?

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive question (track Claude Code by asking Claude) and corrects it to the real one (track Claude Code on a dashboard).

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: A metric: a number counted over time, like tokens used. Open Telemetry: the open standard Claude Code uses to send those numbers out. A collector: a relay that receives them and passes them on. And Prometheus: a database that keeps the numbers over time and answers queries.

beats.narration_text: Anthropic's Claude Code monitoring guide builds one pipeline. On the left, a Claude Code session. Its numbers run down a pipe into a collector, then into Prometheus, and out onto a Grafana dashboard your team can read.

shot.visual_intent: A kraft terminal block lands at the left ('session'); a pipe draws to the right into a kraft funnel (the collector), on into a tall kraft cabinet (Prometheus), and out to a white board whose grey bars grow ('dashboard').
shot.motion_claim: A kraft terminal block lands at the left ('session'); a pipe draws to the right into a kraft funnel (the collector), on into a tall kraft cabinet (Prometheus), and out to a white board whose grey bars grow ('dashboard').

beats.narration_text: It starts switched off. Sending telemetry to your own backend is opt-in, and the switch is one environment variable: Claude Code enable telemetry, set to one.

beats.narration_text: Before any plumbing, the guide tests the tap. Set the metrics exporter to console, cut the export interval from its default of one minute to one second, and run one prompt with the command claude, dash P. The metrics print right in your terminal.

beats.narration_text: For the real pipeline, the guide ships a Docker Compose file. One command, docker compose up, starts three containers: an Open Telemetry collector, Prometheus, and Grafana, which draws the dashboards.

shot.visual_intent: The printout clears and the terminal shrinks to the left; a long dark plinth draws; three pieces drop onto it one by one: the funnel ('collector'), the cabinet ('Prometheus'), the board ('Grafana').

beats.narration_text: Then point Claude Code at the collector. Set the metrics exporter to O T L P, the Open Telemetry protocol, over g R P C, and set the endpoint to localhost, port forty-three seventeen. The pipe connects.

shot.visual_intent: A pipe draws from the terminal toward the funnel ('otlp over grpc'); a socket lands on the funnel ('localhost:4317'); the pipe meets it and a check lands.

beats.narration_text: Now each session drips numbers down the pipe. The live docs list eight metrics: sessions, lines of code, pull requests, commits, cost, tokens, code edit decisions, and active time.

shot.visual_intent: Grey metric drops leave the terminal one after another and ride the pipe into the funnel; eight drops line up above the pipe as the voice names them ('8 metrics').
shot.motion_claim: Grey metric drops leave the terminal one after another and ride the pipe into the funnel; eight drops line up above the pipe as the voice names them ('8 metrics').

beats.narration_text: Each drop carries tags. Tokens are split by type: input, output, cache read and cache creation. Tokens and cost also name the model. And by default every metric carries a session I D, so you can slice the numbers later.

shot.visual_intent: One drop grows at the centre and splits into four smaller drops ('type'); a kraft tag on a string hangs from it ('model'); a second tag hangs from every drop ('session.id').

beats.narration_text: Events are a second stream: one record each time something happens, like a prompt or a tool result, sent by a separate logs exporter. The guide's collector has one pipeline, for metrics only, so events would need their own.

shot.visual_intent: Back to the pipe; a second, thinner pipe draws above it ('events'); white slips ride it; at the funnel a grey cap closes it ('metrics only').
shot.motion_claim: Back to the pipe; a second, thinner pipe draws above it ('events'); white slips ride it; at the funnel a grey cap closes it ('metrics only').

beats.narration_text: What stays out: prompt text isn't collected by default, only its length. Raw file contents and code snippets aren't in metrics or events. And your email, attached when you sign in, goes only to the endpoint you set, never to Anthropic.

shot.visual_intent: A white prompt page slides toward the pipe; a grey gate drops and stops it ('prompt text'); only a small ruler slip goes in ('length'); a code page is stopped too; a kraft email tag rides the pipe to the collector ('your endpoint').
shot.motion_claim: A white prompt page slides toward the pipe; a grey gate drops and stops it ('prompt text'); only a small ruler slip goes in ('length'); a code page is stopped too; a kraft email tag rides the pipe to the collector ('your endpoint').

beats.narration_text: Inside the collector, a receiver takes the metrics in on port forty-three seventeen. A batch step groups them, with a one-second timeout, and a Prometheus exporter sets them out on port eighty-eight eighty-nine.

shot.visual_intent: The funnel grows at the centre; drops enter at the left ('4317'), gather in a grey batch tray ('batch'), and leave by a spout at the right onto a small shelf ('8889').
shot.motion_claim: The funnel grows at the centre; drops enter at the left ('4317'), gather in a grey batch tray ('batch'), and leave by a spout at the right onto a small shelf ('8889').

beats.narration_text: Prometheus isn't sent anything. It scrapes: every fifteen seconds, it pulls from the collector's port eighty-eight eighty-nine and files each number as a time series.

shot.visual_intent: The funnel shrinks to the left with drops waiting on its shelf; the cabinet stands at the right; a grey arm reaches out and pulls the drops in, three times ('scrape', 'every 15 s'); each pull fills a drawer.
shot.motion_claim: The funnel shrinks to the left with drops waiting on its shelf; the cabinet stands at the right; a grey arm reaches out and pulls the drops in, three times ('scrape', 'every 15 s'); each pull fills a drawer.

beats.narration_text: You ask it questions in Prom Q L. The names change shape on the way in: claude code dot token dot usage becomes claude code token usage tokens total. Add it up by type, and one total splits into input, output, cache read and cache creation.

shot.visual_intent: The cabinet at the left; its top drawer slides out; the metric name lands above ('claude_code_token_usage_tokens_total'); one grey column rises, then splits into four columns ('by type').

beats.narration_text: Grafana, on port three thousand, draws the dashboard from the guide's own file: total cost, active users, tokens, lines of code, and cost by model. The cost figures are approximations; for billing, the docs point you to your API provider.

shot.visual_intent: The white board fills the stage ('Grafana'); four stat tiles fill with grey bars one by one, then a chart grows; a grey approximately sign lands on the cost tile ('approximate').

beats.narration_text: For a whole team, an administrator sets the same variables once, in managed settings. A repository's own settings can't turn telemetry on or change where it goes.

shot.visual_intent: A white settings page at the top ('managed settings'); four small terminals in a row; grey lines draw from the page to each, and their lamps light; a kraft repo folder's own line stops short at an ink cross ('repo settings').

beats.narration_text: Last, the report. The guide's script pulls totals from Prometheus with curl and hands them to claude, dash P, which also reads your team's issues through the Linear M C P server, and writes a productivity report.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code. Clone github dot com slash anthropics slash claude code monitoring guide, and start it with docker compose up, dash d. Then run claude, dash P, hello, with Claude Code enable telemetry set to one, O-T-E-L metrics exporter set to O T L P, O-T-E-L exporter O T L P protocol set to g R P C, O-T-E-L exporter O T L P endpoint set to localhost, forty-three seventeen, and O-T-E-L metric export interval set to ten thousand, all in that same command. Query Prometheus at localhost, nine oh nine oh, until a claude code metric arrives, and tell me its name. Then check it yourself. Open localhost nine oh nine oh and search for claude code. Is it there? And start a new session. Does the session count go up by one?

props.command: Clone github.com/anthropics/claude-code-monitoring-guide and start it with docker compose up -d. Then run claude -p "hello" with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1, OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=otlp, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4317 and OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL=10000 set in that same command. Query Prometheus at localhost:9090 until a claude_code metric arrives, and tell me its name.
output: Check: open localhost:9090, search claude_code. There?
Check: start a new session. Session count up by one?
